title: Bench Test Results: Amprius INR21700/50Q (no CCC) - 50A 5000mAh 21700 - Is it 5000Q?
author: Mooch

temperature_points.context: Never exceed the battery’s true continuous discharge rating (CDR), never let it get colder than 0°C or hotter than 60°C to help lower the risks and extend cell life, and keep the plastic wrap and top insulating ring in perfect condition.
The cells I had reached over their 80°C limit at 50A down to 2.5V by a few degrees-C so I’m rating them at 40A true continuous.
The datasheet lists a 125A “max discharge current” rating, temperature-limited to 75°C.
But there was already a lot of voltage sag at 100A so I am giving it a temp-limited (to 75°C) rating of 100A.
Cycle life is listed as >=300 cycles at +5A/-50A to 2.50V or 75°C for a drop to 70% of original capacity.

Charging can be done at a cell temp of -20°C to 70°C in ambient temps of -20°C to 60°C.
This is the first cell that I’ve seen that can be charged when the cell is below 0°C.

temperature_points.context: Never exceed the battery’s true continuous discharge rating (CDR), never let it get colder than 0°C or hotter than 60°C to help lower the risks and extend cell life, and keep the plastic wrap and top insulating ring in perfect condition.
Reliance says you can run it at up to 70A but you must never let it go over 80°C.
Like all cells, at very high current levels it can easily rise another 10°C or more after stopping.
I estimate its true continuous current rating to be about 40A as that would bring the cell up to about 80°C.
If fast charging a lot then I recommend active cooling to keep the cell below 45°C.
